text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT P0 — increased 5xx rate on /v1/generate (canary). PagerDuty: PD-5078. Paging sarah (oncall) and eng-oncall roster. See alert: https://pagerduty.example/PD-5078 :rotating_light:

sarah (oncall): I'm on it. seeing a spike of 502/503 from inference-proxy in canary cluster. Dashboard -> canary region (us-west-2) latency + errors up since ~10m ago.

ajay (backend): I kicked a canary for release/1.8.2 ~12m ago. nothing special in the manifest except a KMS key arg to promote model artifacts.

megan (runtime): logs from runtime: 
```
2026-03-15T15:10:21Z ERROR model-loader DecryptionError: KMS.Decrypt AccessDenied for key alias/redwood-model-v2
2026-03-15T15:10:22Z WARN handle-request failing serving request -> 502
```

leo (ops): also seeing IAM denies on kms:Decrypt for the inference-role. Looks like the key id referenced in the deploy doesn't match the role policy.

ajay (backend): ugh. we rotated the model key yesterday for compliance. CI step updated REDWOOD_KMS_KEY to the new alias during the canary. possible the role binding for the canary nodes wasn't updated.

sarah (oncall): immediate mitigation: disable canary routing and flip feature flag for new-model-routing to fallback. can someone flip the kill-switch? customers are degraded.

megan (runtime): flipping now. Using Console -> Feature Flags -> new-model-routing = off. Also issuing quick routing override to fallback-model for prod-traffic.

deploy-bot: deploy rollback triggered by ajay: rollback release/1.8.2 canary -> release/1.8.1. Command run: `deploy rollback --env prod --service inference --to-tag 1.8.1`

ajay (backend): rolling back, but note: some in-flight pods still try to decrypt artifacts and are failing while warm-up continues. That's why errors persist for a few minutes.

leo (ops): found mismatch in the env var in the canary RC: 
```
# manifest snippet
env:
  - name: REDWOOD_KMS_KEY
    value: "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/6a7b8c9d-OLD"
# expected to be alias/redwood-model-v2 (the new alias), role policy only allows alias/*
```

ajay (backend): looks like CI wrote the raw key ARN instead of the alias. Our role policy only grants kms:Decrypt for alias/redwood-model-v2 not raw key ARNs (policy was tightened). That caused AccessDenied.

sarah (oncall): so root cause = deploy wrote an unsupported KMS principal/key form into canary env -> canary nodes lacked permission. Mitigations = rollback + flag kill-switch to fallback. Any other customer-facing effects?

megan (runtime): customer impact estimate: affected generation requests routed to canary for ~14 minutes. Rough numbers: ~15 customers saw degraded responses, peak error rate 18% on generate endpoints, median latency for succeeded requests doubled. No secrets were exposed — decrypt attempts failed.

pm-alex: notifying customer success and a subset of the highest-traffic customers. Sending templated note: "We experienced a short degradation due to a canary deployment; we've rolled back and applied a routing fallback. Root cause: KMS key reference mismatch. We will follow up with a timeline and remediation."

ajay (backend): ongoing mitigation steps I'm taking now: 1) add transient IAM binding to canary role to allow both alias and ARN for the key while we fix CI; 2) revert CI change that wrote raw ARN; 3) add pre-deploy validator to reject KMS ARNs that don't match allowed prefixes.

megan (runtime): applied temporary role binding. error rate trending back to baseline. runtime health checks passing.

sarah (oncall): passing primary to ajay for root-cause + postmortem (handoff). I'm going to un-pin from PagerDuty. Handoff note: 15:32 UTC - sarah to ajay.

ajay (backend): taking ownership. timeline notes I'll capture in postmortem doc. immediate action items:
- postmortem owner: ajay
- add canary IAM precheck in CI (reject on mismatch)
- extend canary observability to show KMS Decrypt errors per pod
- update runbook: include KMS alias vs ARN guidance and rollback checklist
- notify infra security to review tightened policies vs deploy UX

sarah (oncall): small follow-up: add a one-line alert rule for repeated kms:Decrypt AccessDenied from model-loader to catch this earlier.

incident-bot: STATUS update -> mitigated (15:46 UTC). Incident channel will be archived and follow-up required.

ajay (backend): quick timeline for PMs/CS: impact window 15:18 - 15:32 UTC (14 minutes). Number of affected customers: ~15 (non-enterprise). No data loss, no PII exposure.

megan (runtime): closing out technical mitigation: rollback complete and routing override removed at 15:50 UTC. final health check green.

ajay (backend): will create postmortem doc and link to a follow-up Slack thread. Owner: ajay. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD tomorrow.

pm-alex: I'll prepare customer-facing messaging once we have the postmortem draft.

sarah (oncall): thanks team. leaving note in runbook: verify KMS alias usage and CI validator. If anything regresses ping me. :thumbsup:
